verdict.rationale: x402 is built for exactly this story. The docs say one line of code makes the server answer unpaid requests with HTTP 402, and the client signs a payment and retries. The CDP Facilitator verifies and settles the payment, with fixed, usage-based (upto) and batch pricing, and the docs explicitly say this works "without checkout pages, subscriptions, or separate billing integrations". Independent operators (124 endpoints at httpay.xyz, the Apiosk gateway) and a live probe of real payable Bazaar listings plus the published npm SDK corroborate it. Missing for 10: evidence that per-call verification latency is acceptable for sub-cent micropayments; one operator settles only after delivering the response to avoid it, which shifts trust to the server.
